diagnosis.hosted_exception: Root43460083439 scheduler traceback was never captured (no VM/log authority). Not claimed as proven hosted exception; the local reproduction below is the same real entry point and matches the captured symptom (scheduler exits, docker restart_count 3->5).
diagnosis.reproduced_cause: SUPPORTED, not proven as the hosted exception: refresh work scales with unrecorded objects, and local CPU e5-large embedding costs ~1.85s/doc (2 CPUs, 300-char docs). Any refresh with more than ~15 new/changed objects (e.g. the 50-increment ingest_completion at 16:34:23) outlives the unchanged 30s request boundary; the unmodified scheduler has no handler, so urllib TimeoutError exits it, docker restarts it ~4s later (30s+4s = the ~34s restart cadence in the retained logs), and each restart's refresh starts ANOTHER server-side run over the same objects because the checkpoint is only recorded after index_documents finishes. Duplicate concurrent embeds starve CPU so no run finishes. Historical stderr/exit code/effective overrides remain irretrievable and are not claimed.

diagnosis.superseded_hypothesis: On a cold search-svc the embedding model integrity hashing + ONNX load (LocalEmbeddingEngine.is_ready) was paid lazily by the first request (readyz probe or the scheduler's first /api/search/index/refresh). On a CPU-limited cold start this exceeds the scheduler's 30s per-request boundary, so urlopen raised TimeoutError, main() had no handler, the process exited and docker restart:unless-stopped looped it. Also the compose readyz healthcheck has a 5s timeout and hit the same cold cost.
diagnosis.withdrawn_hypothesis: Cold-model-vs-30s at first tick (official readyz-before-scheduler order) remains disproven; startup warmup removed.

store_snapshot_fix.cause: get_latest ran outside the lock after the locked reload, so a readback reload (which cleared _runs before refilling) could still empty the checkpoint between the writer's reload and get_latest, turning an unchanged refresh into a full rebuild.
store_snapshot_fix.change: index_pipeline.JsonlIndexPipelineStore: reload builds a complete list and publishes it with one assignment (readers never see an emptied list); an in-store RLock serializes reload/record_run/prune file mutation. main.py store_view_lock and wrappers removed; readbacks are plain reload again.
store_snapshot_fix.regression_test: test_unchanged_refresh_stays_incremental_when_readback_reloads_after_writer_reload: reproduces the reviewer interleaving (slow readback reload starts after writer reload returns, before get_latest) and asserts the observable result (is_full_rebuild False, incremental_count 0). Verified to FAIL on the previous index_pipeline.py (full rebuild) and pass now.

retained_checkpoint_empty_or_underfilled.change: IncrementalIndexPipeline.run: on a non-full run with a retrieval backend, objects the checkpoint claims but backend.indexed_document_states(tenant, ids) does not report in sync with the canonical desired is_active flag are added to the objects to index (no force-full, only the missing ones). PostgresRetrievalBackend.indexed_document_states is RLS/tenant-scoped and returns {id: is_active} for embedded or tombstoned rows, so deliberately inactive canonical records are not re-embedded every tick (review P2 fix). Backends that cannot report presence keep checkpoint-only behaviour. Failure still raises (503) with no checkpoint recorded.
